claims.text: The initial eutectic high-entropy alloy contains coarse, dual-phase lamellar colonies.
Numerous internal boundaries in the lamellar colonies act as microcrack-initiation sites during room-temperature tension.
Approximately 50% cold rolling followed by short-time annealing will decrease lamellar-colony size.
Approximately 50% cold rolling followed by short-time annealing will narrow the interlamellar spacing.
The treatment will improve interface coherence between the constituent phases.
Lamellar refinement distributes stress more uniformly across both phases.
Lamellar refinement mitigates stress concentrations at internal boundaries.
Improved interface bonding and disruption of microcrack pathways delay crack propagation.
The treatment will increase room-temperature yield strength relative to the unmodified baseline.
The treatment will increase room-temperature ultimate tensile strength relative to the unmodified baseline.
The treatment will increase room-temperature elongation to failure relative to the unmodified baseline.
Excessive annealing can cause grain coarsening and eliminate the proposed benefit.
Excessive deformation can induce damage and eliminate the proposed benefit.
The strength-ductility improvement occurs only within a narrow processing window that preserves phase integrity.
Variations in alloy composition or processing-induced phase reactions may alter the treatment outcome.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as a single processing step, but it explicitly consists of two sequential operations: cold rolling and annealing.
